liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Described as a glorious closer to the second set; Reviewer also rates Morning Dew and Johnny B. Goode as great [6][8][11]
- **Matilda** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Uncle John's Band, That Would Be Something, Matilda and drums with Willie Green are singled out as wonderful; Garcia can almost be heard smiling during it [1][8][16]
- **Here Comes Sunshine** (2 reviews): Called beautiful; the reviewer says the second set is where the show takes off; Reviewer hears some of the worst out-of-tune playing in it [13][17]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Upbeat version jammed about thirteen minutes before steel drums led into Matilda, with an island feel [11]
- **Touch of Grey** (1 review): Praised for nice guitar work and a strong finish [13]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): One note is missed during the song, but it can be heard at the end jam [13]
- **Me and My Uncle** (1 other source): Weir played acoustic guitar on Me and My Uncle and Maggie's Farm [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Disc01,Track01 Touch Of Grey**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track02 Wang Dang Doodle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track03 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track04 Me And My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track05 Maggies Farm**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track06 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc01,Track07 Music Never Stopped**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Disc02,Track01 Tuning**: rare: 6 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-04-05.143121.nak300-cp4.andy-Boedicker.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 158 min [1]
- **gd1995-04-05.sbd.hinko.tetzeli.fix-18097.35258.reflac.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 158 min; rated 3/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Matilda has glitches and splices, and its sound degrades after the first splice [2]
- **gd95-04-05.schoeps.10385.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 164 min; rated 3.67/5 by 14 [3]. Said about its sound: Above-average audience recording, marred by chatter and noises from nearby attendees [3]
- **gd95-04-05.sbd.18097.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 156 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Matrix reviewer finds it not bad sounding, worth streaming rather than downloading [7]

## Around the show

- Attendee camped in a state park outside the city limits [10]
- Remembers a surprisingly clean portable toilet outside the venue; a local joked that this is just Alabama [10]
- Fans were unsure what time it was, not knowing Alabama's time zone [10]
- The show was short, so fans were back on Birmingham's tie-dyed streets early [11]
- Seventeen-year-old reviewer spent spring break following the tour instead of going to Texas like classmates [14]
- Reviewer sees it as a looser, happier show after the previous night's arty, odd performance [6]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best shows of 1995 and wishes the soundboard were released [8]
- Says it avoids most of the usual complaints about 1995 shows [9]
- Argues the band was heading in a significant new musical direction despite Garcia's health problems [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-04-05.143121.nak300-cp4.andy-Boedicker.flac1644**: taped by Dave Boedicker; transferred by Dave Boedicker; source: Nakamichi 300 Mics W/CP4 Shotguns>Sony TC-D5M Cassette Deck(Lead Deck)>Sony WM-D6C Cassette Deck> Master Tape(Maxell XL-II S 90 And TDK MA-X 100 Minute… [1]
- **gd1995-04-05.sbd.hinko.tetzeli.fix-18097.35258.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Darryl Hinko and Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD > ? > Cassette > CDr with AUD patches [2]. Also: Soundboard source with the start of Here Comes Sunshine patched in from an audience recording; Loud right-channel pops in the audience patch were fixed by replacing that channel with the left [2]
- **gd95-04-05.schoeps.10385.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Paul B. and Chris Larson; source: Audience: Schoeps MK4's [3]. Also: Audience recording made with Schoeps microphones, circulated as a shnf set [3]
- **gd95-04-05.sbd.18097.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > ? > Cassette > CDr with AUD patches via Darryl Hinko [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Robbi Cohn: [1995-04-05 Jefferson Civic Center Coliseum, Birmingham, AL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1995-04-05-jefferson-civic-center-coliseum-birmingham-al-usa/) [19]
